fact: ITU technical assistance project 9UGA21008 (CHF 1,651,100, about US$1.82m, January 2021 to December 2023, status completed) supported Uganda's Ministry of ICT and National Guidance and NITA-U in formulating a 'National ICT Development Strategy'; the document does not say the strategy was adopted, and gives no date of its own so the published year 2021 is used.

ITU committed CHF 1,651,100 (US$1,816,210 estimated) to the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance and NITA-U for strategy formulation and capacity building over 2021-2023; no domestic budget line is stated; date is the published year 2021.

The NITA-U terms of reference (August 2026) cite a 'Draft National ICT Policy, 2022' as the source for the ICT sector's 9 percent GDP share and 2.3 million jobs, so a 2022 draft existed; the document dates no adoption.

The study's authors state that the absence of strong national ICT policy frameworks in Uganda has worsened inadequate use of electronic medical records and call for national ICT policies to be developed; the document gives no date for this beyond its publication date (2025-10-10).
The DIAL case study describes Uganda's enabling environment as starting with its National ICT Policy of 2003 and continuing through 2023, when the Digital Transformation Roadmap was launched.
The Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 (September 2022) lists the overall National ICT Policy 2014 among Uganda's key policies, 'being reviewed'.

The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance Q4 FY2021/22 report states National ICT Policy drafting was completed and awaiting presentation to and approval by Cabinet; the output, first titled National Digital Transformation Policy, was retitled National ICT Policy per the Cabinet Secretariat.

The report shows the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance (E-Services department, Enabling Policies output) running the National ICT Policy's regulatory impact assessment, drafting and Cabinet submission.

The report shows UShs 249.775 million spent by the E-Services department on the output covering the National ICT Policy and the National Cyber Security Strategy (wage UShs 177.025 million, non-wage UShs 72.75 million), in a GoU vote; the spend is shared by both outputs.
